article_content: Johannesburg, South Africa (CNN) -- England's Football Association has formally complained to the World Cup organizers after an England fan gained access to the team's dressing room, a spokesman said on Saturday. Club England Managing Director Adrian Bevington confirmed the fan entered the dressing room on Friday at Green Point Stadium in Cape Town, where England played Algeria to a goalless draw. 'There's been no serious harm done,' he told reporters. 'We're formally taking it up with FIFA; it is now a matter for FIFA.' FA spokesman Mark Whittle told CNN, 'We can confirm the fan entered the England dressing room last night, and we have reported the incident to FIFA.' He said the fan wasn't in the dressing room for long and that no one was harmed. Whittle described the breach as 'not acceptable.' British news outlets reported that the breach occurred moments after Princes William and Harry had left the dressing room. A FIFA official escorted the fan from the premises, according to the South African Police Service, which launched an investigation.

article_content: Swine flu may be inspiring fear worldwide, but for Stephan Zielinski of San Francisco, California, it inspired a song. The genes underlying swine flu inspired one amateur musician to compose music based on it. The virus is classified as H1N1 because it includes two key viral proteins, hemagglutinin (H) and neuraminidase (N). Zielinski, a 41-year-old writer, photographer, computer programmer, and blogger, took the genetic sequence of a variant of hemagglutinin and created a computer algorithm to turn it into music. He's fascinated that despite biologists mapping the genome and predicting the hemagglutinin protein's structure, the human body can't distinguish it as the 'bad guy' until there's a vaccine. Using self-created and commercial computer programs, Zielinski assigned instruments and musical notes to various properties of the protein. He assigned different instruments to categories of amino acids: piano, organ, low synthesizer, and percussion. The melody was created by assigning notes to specific amino acids, with each beat corresponding to an amino acid. The work took about six hours. Zielinski learned of the sequence through an immunologist friend at the Mayo Clinic. Although the mystery of the virus didn't reveal itself musically, the result is a curiously melodic and somewhat soothing work. Dr. Jay Steinberg, an infectious disease specialist at Emory University Hospital Midtown in Atlanta, Georgia, described it as 'nice ambient music' reminiscent of Brian Eno.

article_content: Seoul, South Korea (CNN) -- A cyber attack on Friday morning targeted 40 South Korean websites, including several government agencies and major banks, according to the country's internet security agency. The government detected the first wave of the attack on Thursday, which was coordinated from outside South Korea using 'zombie' computers to slow down or paralyze the operation of designated websites. The attack, known as a DDoS (distributed denial-of-service) attack, involved infected computers directing a massive traffic surge to targeted websites. By Friday, South Korea's leading security software company, AhnLab, had developed a free anti-virus program to treat infected computers after receiving reports of the attack from the South Korean government on Thursday. AhnLab warned that another attack was expected to hit websites at 6:30 p.m. on Friday. Targeted sites included South Korea's presidential office, the foreign ministry, the defense ministry, and main banking websites. No severe damage was reported, but the government was monitoring the situation closely.

article_content: Chaos erupted on a bullet train north of Tokyo when a passenger's bottle of chemical liquid accidentally leaked from his bag, burning four people, including himself and a child, and making at least two others ill. The incident began when a stranger alerted the 40-year-old man, an employee of a geological survey company, that something was leaking from his bag. As he picked up the bag to move, a 5-year-old boy slipped and fell onto the liquid, burning his skin. The boy's parents were burned while trying to help him. The owner of the liquid was also injured, and a woman in her 30s and a train employee felt unwell, likely due to vapor inhalation. Passengers were evacuated from the train at JR Sendai Station in Miyagi Prefecture after a smoke-like haze was detected during a crew inspection. A 48-year-old man on the platform reported seeing a black bag emitting smoke near the carriage doors. The authorities confirmed that 'no lives are in danger.'

article_content: An Oakland neighborhood is in shock after an 8-year-old girl was killed and two young children were injured when an apartment was left riddled with bullets on Wednesday night. Alaysha Carradine, 8, was killed and two of her friends, Amara York, 7, and her 4-year-old brother, were hospitalized when a gunman opened fire on the house they were in at about 11:15 Wednesday night. York's 63-year-old grandmother was also shot in the leg, but her injuries are non-life-threatening. Khamel Hardin, 22, who was upstairs at the time of the attack, went unharmed. Police have not yet released the names of the other victims. 'It was like a bomb, an explosion, just going off so quick,' Hardin told the San Francisco Chronicle. The attack occurred when York ran to answer the doorbell, thinking it was her mother. Instead, she was met with a hail of bullets but survived. Bullets tore through both the security door and the wooden door behind it, as well as the walls of the apartment and a back window; blood was visible on the carpet inside. Carradine was at the apartment because her mother was away on vacation in Washington, D.C. Jesse Fowler, 24, the girl's stepfather, was left to tell the dead 8-year-old's mother the terrible news. 'I just want to know why you would shoot up a house full of kids. Where do you get the satisfaction in that?' Fowler asked local reporters. 'I know the kids didn't do anything to deserve this,' Sharon Smith, who was watching Carradine and let her stay over at York's house, told multiple local reporters, adding 'it's just heartbreaking.' Carradine loved school, reading, and modeling. She was planning to go to a modeling competition with York on Thursday afternoon. Interim Oakland Police Chief Sean Whent and Mayor Jean Quan visited the two injured children at a local hospital on Thursday. Officials have not named any suspects but have announced a $25,000 reward for any information leading to an arrest.

article_content: Editor's note: We asked readers to weigh in on CNN.com Live producer Jarrett Bellini's vacation destination, and you chose South Africa. Check back for updates on his trip. Giraffes are a common sight in Kruger National Park. KRUGER NATIONAL PARK, South Africa (CNN) -- I spent two nights sleeping under a full-moon sky in my hammock at Kruger National Park. Our guides provided tents, but I decided to sleep in the open bush. I survived the night, and it was magnificent. Kruger National Park fit my idea of the African savannah perfectly -- arid and brown from the winter dry season, with low trees and dusty earth that reflected stunning reds and oranges in the early sun. Our guide, Elson, a self-proclaimed African bushman, had an amazing connection with the land and animals. He could spot animals like leopards from a distance. Kruger National Park is roughly the size of Israel, and many animals roamed near the roadside. The animals were in their natural habitat, and we were just passing guests. Giraffes ate high branches, elephants walked across the road fearlessly, and rhinos were present. The zebras played, hippos splashed in the water, and baboons entertained us. As we left, a couple of giraffes and elephants bid us farewell by the roadside.

PARKGA QARANKA EE KRUGER, Koonfur Afrika (CNN) -- Waxaan ku seexday laba habeen oo hoos imaanaysa iftiinka dayaxa, waxaan ku jiifay hammockgayga Parkga Qaranka ee Kruger. Parkga Qaranka ee Kruger wuxuu le'egyahay dalka Israa'iil, xayawaano badanina waxay ku soo dhowaadeen waddooyinka. Xayawaanku kuma jiraan qafisyo; waxay ku jireen deegaanadooda dabiiciga ah, annaguna waxaan aheyn cid aan soo booqanayna. article_content: An Iranian court has sentenced two female journalists, Niloufar Hamedi and Elaheh Mohammadi, to up to seven years in prison for 'collaborating' with the US government. Hamedi received a seven-year sentence, and Mohammadi received a six-year sentence. The charges included 'collaborating with the hostile American government,' 'colluding against national security,' and 'propaganda against the system.' The journalists were awarded the UN's top press freedom prize in May.

Bate was jailed for four years after admitting conspiracy to steal following a year-long crime spree involving over 20 burglaries and thefts. He wrote to One Stop's bosses while on remand, apologising and offering his services to improve security. Teesside Crown Court heard that One Stop was considering his offer despite his criminal history.

article_content: A study published in Genome Research found that the bacteria in human saliva is similar across different geographic locations. Researchers analyzed saliva samples from 120 healthy individuals from 11 countries. The human salivary microbiome doesn't vary significantly between different populations. Streptococcus is the most common type of bacteria found in saliva. Saliva contains more DNA than blood, including bacterial DNA.

article_content: The Brazilian military announced late Friday that they're discontinuing the search for the remains of passengers and crew from Air France Flight 447, which crashed into the Atlantic Ocean on June 1. The decision comes after search teams located wreckage from the flight last week. So far, 51 out of 228 individuals who lost their lives have been found, alongside over 600 pieces of the aircraft and luggage. The recovered remains were handed over to Brazilian authorities for identification, while debris and luggage were given to French investigators. Despite halting the search for bodies, ships remain in the area to locate the flight data recorders, crucial for understanding the cause of the disaster. The wreckage lies approximately 15,000 feet deep, amidst underwater mountains and sea debris. A French submarine and other vessels are using locator beacons to find the black boxes.

article_content: Pulling teeth can be painful, but this brave child does it with determination. Little Striker Stanger from Harrisville, Utah, attached a piece of string to a milk tooth and tied it to his remote control car. He then accelerated the vehicle at full speed, and the stunt was caught on camera. At the beginning of the video, Striker's mother asks him to explain what he's doing. 'I'm going to use this remote to make the truck go all the way to dad... and see if I can pull my tooth out,' he says calmly. Striker then prepares to do the deed, exclaiming: 'OK. Ready, set, booster ignition!' The youngster presses the ignition button on his remote while sitting with his mouth wide open. The truck speeds forward, pulling Striker's tooth out. 'Oh my gosh, it worked!' he exclaims, then runs towards the camera to show off his new 'gummy grin.' The DIY dentistry took less than a minute. Many viewers have praised Striker's bravery and creativity. 'What a great idea! I might have to try your method,' one commenter said.

article_content: Researchers in Finland are on the verge of recreating a beer recipe from the 1840s thanks to a remarkable shipwreck discovery off the Aland Islands in the Baltic Sea. The ship, believed to have sunk during the 1840s, was found in 2010 and contained bottles of beer and champagne that have been remarkably preserved. Analysis of the beer by Finnish researchers revealed that it had retained a pale golden color and may have originally had hints of 'rose', 'almond', and 'cloves'. 'With the chemical analysis we've done and the help of a master brewer, we believe it's possible to create a beer that closely resembles the original,' said Annika Wilhelmson from VTT technical research centre of Finland.

Falanqaynta cabbeereed ee ay ayagu sameeyeen cilimiiriyaasha Finland ayaa muujisay in ay hayso midab dahabi ah oo daciif ah oo laga yaabo in uu hore u lahaa calaamadaha 'rose', 'almond', iyo 'cloves'. 'Iyadoo falanqaynta kiimikada ee aan sameynay iyo caawimaada cagasha cabbeereed ee khabiirka ah, waxaan rumaysanahay in suuragal tahay in la sameeyo cabbeereed si la mid ah asalka ah,' ayaa tiri Annika Wilhelmson oo ka tirsan xarunta cilmi baarista farsamada ee VTT ee Finland.

article_content: Cybersecurity researchers warn that a bug in Apple's iOS operating system makes most iPhones and iPads vulnerable to cyberattacks. The bug, known as 'Masque Attack,' enables hackers to access devices by tricking users into installing malicious applications. FireEye advises users to follow three rules: don't install apps from sources other than Apple's official App Store, avoid clicking 'Install' on pop-ups from third-party websites, and immediately uninstall apps flagged by iOS as 'Untrusted App Developer.'

Cilladda 'Masque Attack' waxay ogolaataa hackers-ka inay galaan aaladaha iyagoo ku qancinaya isticmaalayaasha inay rakibaan codsiyada xaasidnima ah. FireEye waxay ku talinaysaa isticmaalayaasha inay raacaan xeerar: ha isticmaalin apps ka yimaada meelaha aan ahayn Apple App Store, iyo ha ku rakibin apps-ka aan la amin ahayn.

article_content: YAOUNDE - Unrest on the border with Nigeria has severely disrupted the education of thousands of young people in Cameroon, with reports suggesting that Boko Haram is receiving external support. Many Cameroonian schools on the border with Nigeria's Borno state have remained closed as other schools in the country reopen Monday after the Christmas vacation. Some of the schools were either destroyed by Boko Haram fighters or the Cameroon Air Force when they bombarded villages and towns that had been seized by suspected Boko Haram fighters last week, leading to a significant humanitarian crisis. Mbane Wilson, an official of Cameroon's Ministry of Basic Education in northern Cameroon, says thousands of teachers, students and pupils have fled schools located along the border due to bloody confrontations between the Cameroon military and suspected Boko Haram militants, describing it as a 'dire situation'. 'Its a very difficult situation for learners and teachers as many of the schools, especially of the basic education sector, have been closed down due to the conflict with Boko Haram,' explained Wilson. 'We face the attack of Boko Haram and the constant fear of surprises,' he added. Fopa Faison, 19, now an upper sixth student of the Government High School Maroua in northern Cameroon, says he escaped when Cameroon's air force destroyed his old school on the border with Nigeria, and is now 'traumatized'. 'I am praying that things should change [be different] so that we can still live our lives here [in peace here],' said Faison. Faison's uncle, Alain Ngapoue, who also escaped from Ashigashia with his four children, says their school and huge portions of their town were destroyed by rockets launched by Cameroon's air force against suspected Boko Haram fighters who had occupied the area. He says they still have confidence in the Cameroon military that is working to secure their home areas. Maimounatou Farrida, a student from government Bilingual High School Maroua in Cameroon, says their classrooms are now congested with students fleeing the assaults in the border areas near Nigeria. She says their peers from the war zone should be courageous as they prepare their future in their new schools. Last week, Cameroon said its military had launched rockets on at least 1000 suspected Boko Haram fighters who attacked a military base in the border area of Amchide and seized a huge portion of Cameroon's town of Ashigashia and a number of villages. In a telephone interview with VOA, journalist Samuel Sawalda, who is based in northern Cameroon says the affected areas are being deserted by the residents. 'Many schools in areas that share a border with Nigeria, from Lake Chad to the area of Burha in Mayo Tsanaga, have been closed down,' stated Sawalda. 'People have deserted and are still deserting to find refuge in the hinterlands,' he added.

Dugsiyada badan ee Cameroonian ee xadka la leh Nigeria's Borno state ayaa wali xidhnaa iyadoo dugsiyo kale oo dalka ku yaal ay dib u furmaan Isniinta kadib fasaxyadii Christmas. Qaar ka mid ah dugsiyada waxaa burburiyay dagaalyahannada Boko Haram ama Ciidanka Cirka ee Cameroon markay weerareen magaloyinka iyo tuuloyinka ay qabsadeen dagaalyahannada Boko Haram toddobaadkii hore, taasoo horseeday xaalad bini'aadantinimo oo daran. Mbane Wilson, oo ah sarkaal ka tirsan Wasaaradda Waxbarashada Aasaasiga ah ee Cameroon ee waqooyi Cameroon, ayaa sheegay in kuntaan macalimiin, arale iyo aralayaal ah ay ka carareen dugsiyada ku yaal xadka sababtoo ah iskahorimaadyo dhiigaan oo u dhaxeeya ciidanka Cameroon iyo dagaalyahannada Boko Haram, isagoo ku tilmaamay 'xaalad aad u xun'. 'Waxaa jira xaalad aad u adag oo aralayaasha iyo macalimiinta ay wajahayaan maadaama dugsiyada badankood, gaar ahaan waxbarashada aasaasiga ah, ay xidhmaan sababtoo ah iska horimaadka Boko Haram,' ayuu yiri Wilson. 'Waxaan wajahnaa weerarrada Boko Haram iyo cabsi joogto ah,' ayuu yiri. Fopa Faison, oo ah arale oo 19 jir ah oo hadda dhigta dugsi sare oo dawlad ah Maroua waqooyi Cameroon, ayaa sheegay inuu baxsaday markii ciidanka Cirka ee Cameroon ay burburiyeen dugsigii hore ee uu ku jiray xadka Nigeria, isaga oo hadda 'naxsan'. 'Waxaan rajaynayaa in waxyaabaha ay isbeddelaan si aan nolosheenna halkan ku noolaan karno [nabadgelyo],' ayuu yiri Faison. Aalain Ngapoue, oo ah adeerkii Faison, kaas oo sidoo kale ka baxsaday Ashigashia isaga iyo afarta caraha ah, ayaa sheegay in dugsigoodii iyo qaybo badan oo magaladooda ah ay burburiyeen gulan lagu riday ciidanka Cirka ee Cameroon oo weeraray dagaalyahannada Boko Haram ee meesha qabsaday. Wuxuu sheegay inay wali kalsoon yihiin ciidanka Cameroon oo ka shaqeynaya inay sugaan xoolahooda.
